title: Count Letters, Digits, Spaces and Others
statement: Read one line of text. Count its letters, digits, spaces and other characters. Use the functions isalpha, isdigit and isspace from ctype.h. A character that is none of these three is "other". Punctuation marks and symbols are "other". Print the four counts on one line, separated by single spaces, in this order: letters, digits, spaces, others.
inputFormat: One line of text. It has only printable ASCII characters (codes 32 to 126). It may contain spaces.
outputFormat: Four integers on one line, separated by single spaces: letters digits spaces others.
constraints: The line does not end with a space.
Read the whole line, not just one word.
explanations: Hello World has 10 letters. 123 gives 3 digits. There are 2 spaces and no other characters.
The letters are C, i, s, f, u, n. There are 2 spaces. The exclamation mark is the 1 other character.
